unit: percentile of the field's own root-zone wetness (NASA POWER GWETROOT) for the same calendar month, all years of the record (D42)
appliesTo: drought check for every crop in its sensitive months; a month below this percentile counts as drought
sourceTitle: borrowed from U.S. Drought Monitor, Drought Classification
sourceLocator: table 'Percentile Range for Most Indicators': D1 Moderate Drought = 10.01 to 20.00, listed next to SPI/SPEI values. The Drought Monitor applies percentiles to its own indicators; applying the D1 bound to NASA POWER root-zone wetness (GWETROOT) is our mapping. Same calendar month (D42): WMO SPI User Guide (WMO-No. 1090, 2012), PDF p. 13, 'a 1-month SPI at the end of November compares ... November in that particular year with the November precipitation totals of all the years on record'; excerpt in data/samples/rules/wmo-spi-user-guide-2012.txt

sourceTitle: NASA POWER parameter dictionary (community AG, monthly)
sourceLocator: GWETROOT 'Root Zone Soil Wetness': proportion of water in the upper 1 m of soil, 0 dry to 1 saturated

unit: NASA POWER parameter id, °C, read daily
appliesTo: heat check against each crop's own threshold in data/crops: days of the month whose daily maximum is above the threshold are counted (D43, hazards.heat.minDays)
sourceTitle: NASA POWER parameter dictionary (community AG, daily)
sourceLocator: T2M_MAX 'Temperature at 2 Meters Maximum', units C, temporal DAILY: 'The maximum hourly air (dry bulb) temperature at 2 meters above the surface of the earth in the period of interest' (data/samples/power/parameters-tmax-daily.json); the daily point API returns one value per day (data/samples/power/point-daily-tmax-2023-2024-ag.json)

unit: days per month with daily T2M_MAX above the crop's heat threshold
appliesTo: heat check for every crop and the field summary: a month counts as a heat month when at least this many days pass the threshold (D43)
sourceTitle: Steduto et al. (eds.), Crop yield response to water, FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 66, FAO 2012 (barley chapter)
sourceLocator: book p. 139 (PDF p. 154): high temperatures above 30-32 °C shorten grain filling; 'The effect is noticeable even if periods of high temperature are short (even only 3 days).' Second source for field pea: Saskatchewan Pulse Growers, 'A few days of heat above 29°C in the field causes flower and young pod abortion'. Team rule: one value for all crops (D43); excerpts in data/samples/research/agronomy/hf-fao66-crop-chapters.txt and hf-saskpulse-pea-heat.txt
checkedBy: O1, team rule on the saved excerpts, Sat 14 Nov 2026

unit: NASA POWER parameter id, days per month
appliesTo: frost check against each crop's own threshold in data/crops
sourceTitle: NASA POWER parameter dictionary (community AG, monthly)
sourceLocator: FROST_DAYS 'Frost Days': 2 m temperature cools to the dew point and both are below 0 °C

appliesTo: calendar strip: a month cell gets a hazard mark when the crop in the ground is sensitive and the hazard occurred in more than this share of years
sourceLocator: SPEC section 8, calendar strip; value set by the team, shown on screen as a rule of thumb

unit: GAEZ v4 crop suitability index (SI), scale 0-100; the check is "at or below"
appliesTo: crops with SI at or below this value at the field (classes 'Very marginal', 'Not suitable', 'No cultivation') are excluded before scoring; the id keeps 'Below' because the engine reads it
sourceTitle: FAO GAEZ v4 res05 ImageServer legend, renderer 'Crop Suitability Index in Classes - All Land in Grid Cell'
sourceLocator: legend classes: 'SI > 10 : Marginal', 'SI > 0 : Very marginal', 'Not suitable'; SPEC section 7 excludes below 'Marginal'

unit: lower SI bound per GAEZ class, scale 0-100, exclusive ('SI > bound'); notSuitable means SI = 0. Labels: veryHigh 'Very high', high 'High', good 'Good', medium 'Medium', moderate 'Moderate', marginal 'Marginal', veryMarginal 'Very marginal', notSuitable 'Not suitable'
appliesTo: labels for GAEZ suitability on cards and in gaps. Where GAEZ ships a class raster (data/precomputed/gaez.json suitabilityClass), that class wins: it comes from the suitability distribution in the grid cell (GAEZ v4 Model Documentation, Table 7-4) and can differ from these bounds applied to the average index
sourceTitle: FAO GAEZ v4 res05 ImageServer legend, renderer 'Crop Suitability Index in Classes - All Land in Grid Cell'
sourceLocator: legend labels 'SI > 75 : Very high' ... 'SI > 0 : Very marginal'

unit: °C, daily maximum 2 m air temperature (NASA POWER daily T2M_MAX); a month with at least hazards.heat.minDays days above this counts as a heat month
appliesTo: field summary and calendar for months without a crop-specific threshold; crops in data/crops carry their own thresholds, which win
sourceLocator: D26: one crop-independent value, team rule of thumb. Matches the crop thresholds already sourced in data/crops (maize, soybean, potato 35 °C; winter wheat 34 °C)

unit: frost days per month (NASA POWER FROST_DAYS); a month with more than this counts as a frost month
appliesTo: field summary and calendar for months without a crop-specific threshold; crops in data/crops carry their own thresholds, which win
sourceLocator: D26 and #79 item 7: one crop-independent value, team rule of thumb. 0 marked every April in Iowa as a frost month (NASA POWER, Ames 1981-2025: April has frost days in 45 of 45 years). More than 10 frost days (a third of the month) separates frosty springs: April in 14 of 45 years at Ames and 6 of 45 at the Poznań field; March stays a frost month in most years at both. Crop rows in data/crops keep their own stage limits (R10), which win
